newsitem.title: UK: IPE says monitoring Nov gas oil delivery closely.
newsitem.headline: IPE says monitoring Nov gas oil delivery closely.

text.p: International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) chief executive Lynton Jones said on Wednesday the exchange was closely monitoring the delivery of the November gas oil futures contract to ensure performance by the dominant short and long.
"We are closely monitoring what is going on and are in contact with the parties," Jones said by telephone.

A duel between the dominant short, Monte Carlo-based AIC, and the main long, Swiss-based Cargill International SA, on the November contract involves the bulk of the record 865,1000 tonnes physical delivery.
An AIC trader has said Cargill has been excessively slow to take delivery of 627,800 tonnes of the oil on the Rotterdam region barge market.
Cargill has declined to comment on the AIC charges but they have been repeatedly dismissed by traders familiar with Cargill's position.
The delivery must be made over November 16-30, split into three five day periods with the first period expiring at midnight on Wednesday.
Jones said: "We monitor each of these (five-day) periods to make sure performance has taken place. In case of any allegation that performance has not taken place we clearly have an interest.
"So if there is a technical default, either party can refer the matter to arbitration. The (IPE) directors then have to determine the price at which the products will be invoiced back."
Jones added that in some cases the price could include a premium to reflect compensation for the aggrieved party.

Traders have said Cargill established a large long position in November futures and bet that AIC, which has a large short position, would not be able to deliver into its commitments and therefore buy back its position at a higher price.

Jones, giving a hypothetical example of what he called a potential complication, added that if a delivery had not taken place by midnight on the last day of a delivery period and a barge was ready in position but was unable to load because some sort of technical holdup then the delivery period might "be extended for up to two days".
Some traders say arbitrations over delivery disputes can last for one year or more.
